questions.question: Drivers stuck behind a slow vehicle often:
questions.explanation: Many drivers tailgate slow vehicles. If someone tailgates you, let them pass safely.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts usually means they are loose.

questions.question: Check your mirrors:

options.text: Only when other vehicles are nearby.
Only when it is dark outside.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before changing lanes. Regular mirror checks should be part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: To apply for a CDL, you must be at least:
questions.explanation: In California, you must be at least 18 years old to apply for a commercial driver license.

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you must back up, you should:

options.text: Get out and walk around to know the area better.
Not use both side mirrors because it can be distracting.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can watch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to know the area better.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of your vehicle and look at your path. Check for space on the sides and overhead.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. The valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: Cargo needs one tie-down for every ____ of cargo length.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine slows down.
Push the clutch out when the engine slows down.
Shift into neutral when the engine slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine slows down.
questions.explanation: Apply steady brake pressure and stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine slows down.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: Unbalanced loads cause unsafe handling. Distribute cargo weight evenly when loading your vehicle.

questions.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads is to:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, hydroplaning is more likely if tire pressure is low or tread is worn. If you hydroplane, release the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog if possible.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Avoid it if you can. If you must drive in fog, turn on your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts at the crossing. Call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal activates while driving, you should:

options.text: Exit the road and park as soon as you can safely do so.
Stop immediately and park where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as you can safely do so.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal activates, safely exit the road and park your vehicle as soon as possible. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, backing toward the driver's side:

options.text: Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when you must reverse. This gives you the best view of your path.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires allowed on a bus?
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus. They are allowed only on the rear.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to make the brakes work?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to operate the brakes.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, you must:

options.text: Have your employer notified by the state.
Notify your employer within two business days.
Notify your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Notify your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: If your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or you are disqualified from driving, you must tell your employer within two business days.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Notify emergency services of your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because it is harder to see hazards in the dark.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always come to a complete stop.
May need to swerve your vehicle out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve your vehicle out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down. Reducing your speed helps you stay safe.

questions.question: Talking on a cell phone while driving removes about ____ of a person's focus from driving.
questions.explanation: Talking on a cell phone while driving removes about 39 percent of your attention from the road. This is a serious distraction.

questions.question: What must be on all air tanks with air-braked vehicles?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have a check valve. It allows air to flow in one direction only and prevents air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.

questions.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.text: Should only be used if a vehicle is close to you.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you signal.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle will still have normal brakes without ABS. Brake as you normally would and have your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.explanation: Pull the slack adjusters to check them. They should not move more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need to be adjusted.

questions.question: When starting your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Quickly jump from low to high.

questions.explanation: After starting your engine, the coolant temperature should slowly increase to the normal operating range.

questions.question: Some air brake systems introduce alcohol into the system to:

options.text: Make the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
Prevent people from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems use an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: If you are taking the driving test and the route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: You should do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time because:

options.text: You will be less likely to forget something.
You will have more time to complete the inspection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Following the same order each time helps you remember all the steps. You are less likely to skip a step when you use a checklist in the same order.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Do not use your brakes until your vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle during a leakage test, the maximum air loss is:
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, the air loss during a leakage test should not exceed 4 psi in a minute. You need to know the safe air loss rate for your specific vehicle.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on your driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior during the on-road driving test.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail while driving downhill, first look for an escape ramp. If there is no ramp, find another place to stop, such as an open field or a side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold only enough air for one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air so the brakes can still be used several times if the compressor fails.

questions.question: In winter, which item needs extra attention during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: During winter, pay extra attention to coolant and antifreeze levels, defrosting and heating equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires, tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, steps, handholds, and the exhaust system.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not be provoked by an angry driver's gestures. Do not make eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: Placards for hazardous cargo must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo so they can be seen from any direction.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up the fuel.

questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine as soon as you safely can. Do not open the hood when putting out the fire.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check where it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check where it is.
questions.explanation: A look happens when a driver opens their door, gets out, and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During the straight line backing exercise, a driver can only do one look. During other exercises, a driver can do up to two looks.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under good driving conditions?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under good conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: Emergency brakes must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. These brakes should use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time.

questions.question: What is a danger of swerving to avoid a hazard while driving a large truck?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.

questions.explanation: Swerving can be safe sometimes, but it has risks. Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers can flip over when swerving.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: Except for the straight line backing exercise, how many times can a driver exit and check the vehicle's position during testing?
questions.explanation: A driver can exit to check the vehicle's position during any test exercise. This is called a look. During straight line backing, a driver can only do one look. During other exercises, a driver can do up to two looks.

questions.question: Every vehicle registered in California must have at least:
questions.explanation: Every registered vehicle in California must have at least two mirrors. One must be on the left side and show the road behind for at least 200 feet.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should the weight be placed?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity is more likely to tip over than cargo with a low center of gravity. Weight should be distributed as low as possible to prevent tipping.

questions.question: If you see a construction worker near the road while driving slowly through a construction zone, you should:
questions.explanation: Always slow down in construction areas. Slow down even more if you see workers on or near the road.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually comes from two causes: loss of hydraulic pressure or overuse on long hills, which causes the brakes to fade.
